name: Universidad de Malaga
overview:
IMPORTANT - ADDITIONAL PROGRAM REQUIREMENTS

Students must demonstrate a B2 level in Spanish via an interview with a Spanish speaker (organized by IAFF team)


______________________________________________________________________________________


Founded in 1987, the Higher Technical School of Computer Engineering of the University of Malaga is a pioneer in the offer of university studies in computer science in Andalusia. Its missions and objectives are to train professionals in all fields of computer engineering.


Recently, the degrees in computer engineering, software engineering and computer engineering of this school have obtained the international quality label EURO-INF, awarded by the European agency EQANIE: http://www.eqanie.eu


For the advice of travelers, click here.
administrative:
1) Application Dossier


Once the IAFF office has sent your nomination, the partner university will contact you directly by email to start your application. All required documents will have to be uploaded on their platform or sent by email before the deadline (see EMEA Teams channel for each application deadline).


If you have not received anything yet, it means your nomination has not been sent yet — please be patient.


To be completed with your Epitech bachelor campus administration during the registration period for Tech4 (usually in April/May):

  • The addendum to the contract.
  • EPITECH re-registration dossier.


2) Visa


For European students, a valid passport or national ID card is sufficient to travel to Europe (exception for the UK).


For non-European students or students with a non-European citizenship, please check the immigration office of the host country to check the visa process and fees.


Students in France can use this website: https://www.diplomatie.gouv.fr/fr/


3) Insurance


For European students


The European Health Insurance Card (CEAM in French) is nominative and individual. This card certifies your rights to the Health Insurance in Europe.


To obtain your card, log in to your Ameli account at least two months before your departure. It is free of charge and will be sent to your place within two weeks. You can also download it online.


More information: https://www.ameli.fr/assure/droits-demarches/europe-international/protection-sociale-etranger/etudes-etranger


For non-European students


You must register for a private health insurance to cover your full stay. Please check with your parents, bank, or any private insurance company for more information depending on the wanted coverage.


Please register via the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Ariane) platform to be aware of any news (terrorist attack, tsunami, earthquake…) in your host country — for French citizens only: https://pastel.diplomatie.gouv.fr/fildariane/dyn/public/login.html
accomodation:
Off-campus Housing :


Shared-flat


Renting a room in a shared apartment with other students is the most popular way of life in Malaga. There are a large number of apartments available for rent, located in different parts of the city, and it usually does not take much time to find one.


UMA does not reserve accommodation for students, but helps them to find a room or apartment through "Welcome to UMA," which must be contacted to have further access to consulting the offers:


Contact details for Welcome to UMA:


Web page: https://www.uma.es/welcome-uma


Email: accommodationuma@uma.es


Temporary accommodation


We recommend to students who have not reserved permanent accommodation before their arrival to find temporary accommodation for a few days. You can click below for more information: http://www.studentrentalmalaga.com


Other options: https://www.idealista.com/


The ESN office (Erasmus Student Network) would be another option. Please contact them at: esn.malaga@gmail.com


In-campus Housing


Housing in university residences


There are also several residences, but unlike many other countries, this option is not very popular among exchange students.


They usually offer meals, laundry services, cleaning and the like, but at the same time, this option is more expensive. Ask the accommodation office for more details.


Web page: http://www.uma.es/alojamiento/


Email: alojamiento@uma.es


https://www.resa.es/es/residencias/malaga/residencia-universitaria-campus-malaga/residencia-malaga/


Homestay accommodation


Another option is to look for accommodation with a Spanish family. This could be particularly beneficial for students who wish to practice their Spanish skills.


When you search for housing, you can also use other resources such as internet searches or personal contacts.
courses:
You must obtain 30 ECTS credits per semester, i.e. 60 ECTS credits over the year.


The Higher Technical School of Computer Engineering 'Escuela Técnica Superior de Ingeniería Informática' is located on the campus Teatinos.


You have to take courses in Spanish at the Higher Technical School of Computer Engineering of the University of Malaga.

  • Materials (slides, etc.) are provided in English.
  • Teachers do not have any problem in answering in English.


Courses start in mid-September, but you must arrive in early September.


End of the 1st semester: at the end of January.


2nd semester: starts in mid-February and ends at the end of June.


You can find the academic calendar here: https://www.uma.es/etsi-informatica/info/73256/calendarios-de-grado/


We do not recommend mixing courses from different programs.


Program 1


Máster Universitario en Ingeniería Informática : https://www.uma.es/etsi-informatica/info/113641/master-u-ingenieria-informatica-nuevo-plan-2018-2019/


Program 2


MÁSTER UNIVERSITARIO EN INGENIERÍA DEL SOFTWARE E INTELIGENCIA ARTIFICIAL https://www.uma.es/etsi-informatica/info/72554/master-ing-del-sw-e-int-artific-plan-estudios/#Plan


Testimonial of a student enrolled in the Máster Universitario en Ingeniería Informática, in 2021–22:

"The first year is rather normal and without any specialities, the courses start at 4.30pm and end at 8.30pm from Monday to Thursday from October to February for the first semester and February to June for the second semester.
The second year is composed of two specialties (Cybersecurity / Data Science and Engineering). The courses start at the end of September and end at the end of December. The classes are worth 4.5 credits each.
Classes start at 4pm and end at 8:45pm."


Attention:


Attendance in class is compulsory. The courses are most likely more academic than at Epitech.


The course list is given to you for information, it can change from year to year.


If a course is not available when you arrive, EPITECH cannot be held responsible for it.
